einzeiler: Moving house, remembering departed friends, and recording the sounds of Irish wildlife.
kurzfassung: The host reflects on moving into a new home and dealing with the bittersweet memories of leaving a self-made wildlife haven. The episode features field recordings and insights into migrating birds, seasonal shifts, and hidden insect sounds. Additionally, the host pays tribute to recently departed cultural figures and friends.
stichpunkte: Moving house after five years and reflecting on the wild border garden created there
Saying goodbye to a rented home where wildflowers and pollinators thrived despite management
Tributes to musician Glenn Hansard and birdwatcher John Lynch
Observing the early autumn migration of swallows, swifts, and wading birds
Audio recordings and identification calls of curlews, gulls, kingfishers, and plovers
A blackbird mimicking the display call of a little ringed plover in Cork
Mystery nature sounds resolved, including dragonfly wing beats, froghopper vibrations, and cockchafer beetles
beschreibung:
This week on The Seán Chorus, Seán Ronayne provides a small update along with more sounds and moments that have made his new home feel familiar.
From the call of the curlew echoing through the balcony door, to capturing the hum of bees and grasshoppers in a wildflower meadow, Seán reflects on more memories and his connection to the natural world. Explore the return of Mediterranean gulls to Cork Harbour, and even a mystery sound challenge, in this latest episode.
This is a HeadStuff podcast produced by Hilary Barry and Dan Wilcox. Original artwork is by Matt Mahon.
